project.name: libarchive
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source inspected here is the bundled libarchive checkout at `64e68f2034e6c5c6fd20d6b274b67fbdb88c3804`, whose `archive_read_support_format_rar5.c` line map matches the saved ASan stack (`parse_file_extra_owner:1377`, `process_head_file_extra:1441`, `process_head_file:1618`, `process_head_service:1670`, `process_base_block:1921`). ARVO metadata separately reports `7b3068c4bf7a217a1838db280072653197d30012` / `2fce6f81cc59144bf4f2f66f7620233d609b41ef` as the vulnerable/fixed commits. The staged worktree is an earlier equivalent RAR5 owner/group parser implementation carrying the same missing `>= OWNER_MAXNAMELEN` truncation obligation, and the staged `patch.diff` fixes that same logic in the later upstream revision.

classification.classification_note: The observed memory error is a 1-byte out-of-bounds stack write: the RAR5 owner parser copies a group name into `char namebuf[256]` and then appends a NUL terminator without reserving space for that terminator when the parsed name length reaches 256.

bug_description.normalized: The staged 357-byte RAR5 witness drives libarchive through `rar5_read_header -> process_base_block -> process_head_service -> process_head_file -> process_head_file_extra`, where the current service header carries an `EX_UOWNER` extra record. `parse_file_extra_owner()` decodes owner flags whose `OWNER_GROUP_NAME` bit is set, then reads an attacker-controlled group-name length and points `p` at that many owner bytes. In the vulnerable code, the group-name clamp treats only `value_len > OWNER_MAXNAMELEN` as oversized and otherwise leaves `name_len = value_len`; once the parsed length is 256 or larger, `name_len` becomes 256 even though `namebuf` is only `char namebuf[256]` and the code still appends a terminator after the copy. `memcpy(namebuf, p, name_len)` fills `namebuf[0..255]`, then `namebuf[name_len] = 0` writes one byte past the stack buffer at line 1377. Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at that exact statement. The staged fix changes both owner-name branches to truncate `>= OWNER_MAXNAMELEN` down to `OWNER_MAXNAMELEN - 1` before writing the terminator.

source.description: First project-code read inside the crashing owner-extra parser that materializes attacker-controlled state used by the vulnerability path.
source.value_from: Stage 01 reproduced the crash on the exact staged 357-byte RAR5 witness. On that path, `process_head_file_extra()` dispatches `EX_UOWNER` to this parser at line 1441, and the later crash at line 1377 proves that the decoded flags make the real group-name predicate at line 1366 evaluate true.
source.note: This read decodes the owner-field flags varint. The later `if ((flags & OWNER_GROUP_NAME) != 0)` check at line 1366 uses this decoded state to select the crashing group-name branch.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The parser appends a NUL terminator one byte past the fixed 256-byte stack buffer.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at `parse_file_extra_owner:1377:21` and identifies `namebuf` as the frame object occupying `[128, 384)`. The invalid write is at offset 384, which is exactly index 256 of `char namebuf[256]`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The group-name clamp allows `name_len` to become 256 instead of reserving one byte for the trailing NUL.
root_cause.note: On the crashing path, the parsed group-name length is large enough that this code leaves `name_len == OWNER_MAXNAMELEN`. The later terminator store at line 1377 therefore targets index 256 of `namebuf[256]`. The staged patch fixes the exact obligation by changing the threshold to `>= OWNER_MAXNAMELEN` and truncating to `OWNER_MAXNAMELEN - 1` before the terminator write.

parser_admitted.description: On the saved crashing path, the current RAR5 FILE/SERVICE extra-field ID decodes as `EX_UOWNER`, so `process_head_file_extra()` enters `parse_file_extra_owner()`. The surrounding stack frames at `process_head_file:1618`, `process_head_service:1670`, and `process_base_block:1921` show that this happens while parsing a RAR5 service header's extra data.

tainted_value_origin.description: This read materializes the attacker-controlled group-name length that later becomes both the copy size and the terminator index.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: On the crashing path, this is the length field of the `OWNER_GROUP_NAME` payload inside the `EX_UOWNER` extra record. The later out-of-bounds write proves that it decodes to a value that makes the vulnerable clamp leave `name_len == OWNER_MAXNAMELEN`.

coarse_trace.summary: The current RAR5 base block is parsed as `HEAD_SERVICE`, and the service-header path delegates to the ordinary FILE-header parser.
The FILE parser sees extra data, decodes the current extra-field ID as `EX_UOWNER`, and dispatches into `parse_file_extra_owner()`.
The owner parser decodes flags, the `OWNER_GROUP_NAME` predicate selects the second owner-name branch, and that branch reads the attacker-controlled group-name length and source pointer.
The vulnerable clamp allows `name_len == 256`, `memcpy()` fills `namebuf[256]`, and the subsequent terminator store at `namebuf[256]` overflows the stack buffer.

fine_trace.note: Source. The owner parser reads the attacker-controlled owner flags varint and stores the decoded bitfield in `flags`. The later group-name predicate at line 1366 makes the vulnerability-relevant control decision from this exact value.
Control step. On the witnessed crashing path, this predicate evaluates true, so execution enters the second owner-name branch instead of skipping it.

Inside the selected group-name arm, the parser reads the attacker-controlled group-name length and obtains `p`, a pointer to that many owner-name bytes. The later clamp, copy, and sink all use this exact length and source buffer.

Root cause. This clamp treats only `value_len > 256` as oversized and otherwise preserves the parsed length. On the witnessed crashing path, the parsed group-name length is large enough that this code leaves `name_len == 256`, so the later terminator write has no in-bounds slot left in `char namebuf[256]`.

The copy uses the attacker-controlled bytes at `p` and the unclamped `name_len` from step 4. With `name_len == 256`, it fills every valid byte of `namebuf[0..255]` and leaves no room for a trailing NUL.

Sink. The parser appends the terminator using the same `name_len` computed in step 4. Because step 5 already filled the 256-byte destination, this store writes one byte past `namebuf`, matching the saved ASan `WRITE 1` at offset 384 in the `namebuf` stack slot.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Yes. The staged `patch.diff` changes both owner-name branches in `parse_file_extra_owner()` from allowing `name_len = OWNER_MAXNAMELEN` to truncating `>= OWNER_MAXNAMELEN` down to `OWNER_MAXNAMELEN - 1`, which is exactly the missing guard on the crashing path.

poc.trigger: Feeding the staged 357-byte `poc` RAR5 archive to the vulnerable Stage 01 `libarchive_fuzzer` reproduces the saved `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow` write of size 1 in `parse_file_extra_owner()`.

format.name: 357-byte RAR5 service header carrying an owner extra record with an oversized group name
format.contract: The witness is a raw RAR5 archive beginning with the standard signature `52 61 72 21 1a 07 01 00`. On the crashing header, `process_base_block()` dispatches a `HEAD_SERVICE` block to `process_head_file()`, `process_head_file_extra()` decodes the current extra-field ID as `EX_UOWNER`, and `parse_file_extra_owner()` takes the `OWNER_GROUP_NAME` branch. The trigger condition is an owner group-name length varint that decodes to at least `OWNER_MAXNAMELEN` (256) with that many bytes available, so the vulnerable clamp leaves `name_len == 256`, `memcpy()` fills `namebuf[256]`, and the subsequent terminator write at `namebuf[name_len]` matches the staged ASan `WRITE 1` at line 1377.
